summary: Generic one-time notification pipeline that persists notification records in Postgres, polls for due records via APScheduler, and dispatches them to Android devices through the FCM HTTP v1 API.

classification.why_platform: Provides reusable notification dispatch capability with no embedded domain logic. The source field is an opaque tag; the platform does not interpret its value. Any application layer component may create, cancel, or replace a notification through the same contract.
non_goals: Rich notification actions beyond the single deep-link tap
Per-source customization of Android notification appearance
Delivery retry policy beyond marking status=failed
Native Android destination screens outside Atlas
Multi-device or per-user device registration table (deferred to a future slice)

consumes: firebase-admin Python SDK for FCM dispatch
FCM service account credential loaded from environment at startup (FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_PATH or FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_CONTENT — never hardcoded)
DATABASE_URL environment variable for Postgres connection
provides: HTTP API at /api/notifications/ for create, cancel, and replace operations
Guaranteed persistence of notification record in Postgres before returning a success response to caller
At-least-once FCM dispatch attempt for every record that reaches status=pending and fire_at <= now()
Maximum expected dispatch latency of ~5 seconds from fire_at (one full polling interval); average ~2.5 seconds. The draft acceptance criterion of 2 seconds is expected-case, not worst-case.
Structured INFO-level log on every dispatch: notification_id, fire_at, dispatched_at, delta_ms
Cancel-by-id semantics: sets status=cancelled, retains record in Postgres, returns success for already-dispatched records (no-op)
invariants: dispatch_due_notifications() only processes records with status=pending — prevents double-dispatch on repeated polls
fcm_token is never exposed in any API response or log output
Notification record contains only generic platform fields — no domain-specific fields from any application
Replace is implemented as two discrete operations: cancel(old_id) then create(new_record) — not an in-place update
Replace is not atomic in this slice: partial failure (old cancelled, new create fails) is a known edge case, not a silent assumption
All API error responses use api_error() from platform_errorhandling — no ad-hoc error formats
FCM credentials are loaded from environment at startup — never read from a config file checked into source control
failure_modes: NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND: cancel or replace called with an id that does not exist in Postgres — 404
FCM_DISPATCH_FAILED: FCM API call returns an error — notification status set to failed, error logged, no retry
FCM_CREDENTIAL_MISSING: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_PATH or FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_CONTENT not set at startup — service fails to start
DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE: Postgres not reachable at startup or during a request — 503 from api_error()
REPLACE_PARTIAL_FAILURE: old notification cancelled successfully, new notification create fails — old record remains cancelled, caller receives error for the create step
CANCEL_ON_DISPATCHED: cancel called on a record with status=dispatched — returns 200 success, no state change, no FCM cancellation attempt
INVALID_FIRE_AT: fire_at is in the past at creation time — accepted and persisted; dispatch job will pick it up on the next poll cycle

provides: NotificationRecord: id (UUID), source (string), fire_at (datetime, UTC), title (string), body (string), label (string), deep_link (string), fcm_token (string, platform-internal), status (enum: pending|dispatched|cancelled|failed), created_at (datetime, UTC)

consumes: psycopg2 connection pool via database.py (same pattern as WorkoutTracker and TaskTracker)
provides: POST /api/notifications/ — create a notification, returns NotificationRecord with generated id
DELETE /api/notifications/{id} — cancel a notification by id, returns 200 on success (including already-dispatched records)
POST /api/notifications/{id}/replace — delete old notification and create new one, returns new NotificationRecord

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/notifications/
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Accept a notification creation request, persist to Postgres with status=pending, return the persisted record including server-generated id

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/notifications/{id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Set notification status to cancelled if pending; return success (no-op) if already dispatched; return 404 if id not found

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/notifications/{id}/replace
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Cancel the notification identified by id (if pending), then create and persist a new notification with the provided fields. Returns the new record. Not atomic — partial failure is surfaced as an error.

exposed_surfaces.name: NotificationService.create
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Internal service method: validate fields, generate UUID, write record to Postgres, return NotificationRecord

exposed_surfaces.name: NotificationService.cancel
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Internal service method: set status=cancelled for pending records; no-op (return success) for dispatched; no-op (return success) for already-cancelled — cancel is idempotent for all terminal states; raise NotFound for missing id

exposed_surfaces.name: NotificationService.replace
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Internal service method: call cancel(old_id) then create(new_payload); propagates errors from either step

exposed_surfaces.name: DispatchJob.dispatch_due_notifications
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Called by APScheduler every 5 seconds: query pending records with fire_at <= now(), send FCM message for each, update status to dispatched or failed, log timing fields

internal_flow.name: startup
internal_flow.description: FastAPI startup event: initialise Postgres connection pool, load FCM service account credential from environment, initialise firebase_admin app, start APScheduler BackgroundScheduler with one IntervalTrigger job (dispatch_due_notifications, interval=5s). Service fails to start if FCM credential environment variable is absent.
outputs: Running APScheduler with dispatch job registered

internal_flow.name: create_notification
internal_flow.description: Caller POSTs to /api/notifications/. Router validates request body against NotificationCreateRequest schema. NotificationService.create generates a UUID, writes a row to notifications.notification with status=pending, returns NotificationRecord. Postgres write completes before response is returned.
outputs: NotificationRecord (id, source, fire_at, title, body, label, deep_link, status=pending, created_at)

internal_flow.name: cancel_notification
internal_flow.description: Caller sends DELETE /api/notifications/{id}. Service looks up record by id. If status=pending, updates to cancelled. If status=dispatched, returns 200 with no state change. If status=cancelled, returns 200 with no state change (idempotent — cancel is a no-op for all terminal states). If not found, returns api_error NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND 404.

internal_flow.name: replace_notification
internal_flow.description: Caller POSTs to /api/notifications/{id}/replace with a new notification body. Service calls cancel(old_id) then create(new_payload). If cancel fails (not found), error is returned before create is attempted. If create fails after cancel succeeds, caller receives an error for the create step; old record remains cancelled.
outputs: New NotificationRecord with new UUID on success

internal_flow.name: dispatch_due_notifications
internal_flow.description: APScheduler fires dispatch_due_notifications() every 5 seconds. Job queries notifications.notification WHERE fire_at <= now() AND status = 'pending'. For each row: builds FCM data-only message from notification fields + fcm_token, calls firebase_admin.messaging.send(), records dispatched_at timestamp, computes delta_ms = (dispatched_at - fire_at) in milliseconds, logs at INFO level: {notification_id, fire_at, dispatched_at, delta_ms}. On FCM success: updates status=dispatched. On FCM failure: updates status=failed, logs error at ERROR level. fcm_token is never logged.
inputs: Pending notification rows from Postgres with fire_at <= now()
outputs: status=dispatched rows for successful FCM sends
ERROR log entry per FCM failure

internal_flow.name: shutdown
internal_flow.description: FastAPI shutdown event: APScheduler BackgroundScheduler is stopped cleanly. In-flight dispatch_due_notifications() calls are allowed to complete (APScheduler default behavior). No durable state is lost — only the in-memory job schedule, which is recreated on next startup.

internal_required.role: Logging setup, FastAPI exception handlers, request timing, api_error() for all error responses

external_required.name: psycopg2-binary
external_required.role: Postgres driver (same pattern as WorkoutTracker and TaskTracker)

external_required.name: APScheduler>=3.0,<4.0
external_required.role: In-process background scheduler for dispatch_due_notifications polling job

external_required.name: firebase-admin
external_required.role: FCM dispatch via Firebase Admin Python SDK

forbidden: Celery (introduces broker dependency disproportionate to this slice — excluded by design_specs.md §1)
Any domain-specific field from WorkoutTracker in the notification schema (violates R-CON-PL-01)
Hardcoded FCM credentials in source (violates R-OPS-BP-02)
Notification platform endpoints embedded in WorkoutTracker router (violates R-CON-PL-01)

persistence.schema_notes: Single table: notifications.notification. Columns: id (UUID PK), source (text not null), fire_at (timestamptz not null), title (text not null), body (text not null), label (text not null), deep_link (text not null), fcm_token (text not null), status (text not null, check constraint: pending|dispatched|cancelled|failed), created_at (timestamptz not null default now()). Index on (status, fire_at) for dispatch query performance.

deferred_decisions: Future: device registration table for multi-device or multi-user FCM token management (per-notification column is used in this slice)
Future: retry policy for failed FCM dispatches (explicitly excluded from this slice)
Future: notification history UI or inbox (excluded from this slice)
Future: recurring notification scheduling (explicitly excluded; identified as next slice candidate in draft)
Future: reduction of poll interval below 5 seconds if worst-case timing tolerance tightens

risks.impact: The 2-second acceptance criterion in the draft is an expected-case figure (average latency ~2.5s with 5s polling). If a human reviewer interprets it as worst-case, the acceptance criterion will not be met. The dispatch log (delta_ms field) provides the evidence needed to evaluate this.

The fcm_token field must never appear in any log line. If the dispatch job logs the full notification row naively, the token is exposed in log files. The implementer must explicitly exclude this field from all log statements.

risks.risk: Non-atomic replace produces orphaned cancelled records
risks.impact: If create fails after cancel succeeds in a replace operation, the old notification is permanently cancelled with no replacement. This is an accepted edge case for MVP but callers must handle the error and retry the full replace if this matters to them.

The atlas:// scheme declared in fcm_payload_contract.json must match the Android intent-filter configuration. If Android Claude uses a different scheme (e.g., https://), tap handling will silently fail. The fcm_payload_contract.json is the authoritative source; Android Claude must not deviate from it.

open_questions.question: Should deep_link validation at create time accept only atlas:// or also https://<atlas-host>/* schemes? The specs allow both but require explicit declaration. This design declares atlas:// only for this slice.

Does the WorkoutTracker call the Notifications platform via HTTP (cross-service) or in-process Python import? This design mandates HTTP API (standalone service) for architectural correctness and future reuse. If WorkoutTracker and Notifications share a Docker network, this requires no external exposure.
